info.title: Map new studio frontend at origin/main (@explore subagent)

parts.text:
Explore the git branch `origin/main` of the repository at /home/alexa/repos/agentic-odi. The frontend lives at `apps/studio/`. Use `git show origin/main:<path>` to read files (the working tree is on an older commit, so you MUST read via git show, not the filesystem).

Goal: produce a precise map of the Living Studio SPA's user-facing structure at origin/main, for writing Playwright E2E tests. Report:

1. **App shell**: Read `apps/studio/src/App.tsx` and `apps/studio/src/main.tsx`. What is the top-level component tree? Is there still a `StudioProvider`/context? Where does it live (e.g. `src/state/`)?

2. **Navigation**: Read `apps/studio/src/components/workspace/WorkbenchRail.tsx`, `apps/studio/src/components/workspace/WorkspacePanel.tsx`, and `apps/studio/src/components/workspace/panels.tsx`. List EVERY distinct view/tab/panel the user can navigate to. For each: the visible label text, the DOM element (button? role? aria-*?), and any test-visible identifiers. Note especially `role=`, `aria-label`, `aria-selected`, `data-*` attributes.

3. **Chat**: Read `apps/studio/src/components/chat/ChatStage.tsx`, `Composer.tsx`, `Conversation.tsx`, `Hero.tsx`, `OfflineNotice.tsx`, `Markdown.tsx`. What are the accessible names/placeholders of the chat input, send button, message bubbles, and any quick-prompt/suggestion buttons? What role does the message log have?

4. **Canvas/outcomes UI**: Is there still an Opportunity Landscape / outcome cards / job map? Search for "Opportunity Score", "Underserved", "outcome-card", "outcome_score". Read whatever renders desired outcomes. Report accessible names for outcome cards, score pills, and any filter/sort checkboxes.

5. **Direct capture / CRUD forms**: Read `apps/studio/src/components/canvas/DirectCapture.tsx` and `JobMap.tsx` and any manual-crud components. Report form field labels (`<label for>`), input types (esp. range inputs), button labels, and success/error toast text.

6. **Settings**: Read `apps/studio/src/components/SettingsPanel.tsx`. Report field labels, buttons, and the toggle for the settings panel.

7. **Toasts/notifications**: Find the toast component. Report the text of success vs error toasts for key actions (capture outcome, add step, sync canvas).

8. **State/data flow**: Read `apps/studio/src/state/*` (whatever files exist) and `apps/studio/src/api/studioApi.ts`. What API endpoints does the SPA call? Does it poll, and on what interval? Does it use a cached value in localStorage? What are the exact fetch paths?

9. **Feature flags**: Read `apps/studio/src/features/flags.ts`. What flags exist and how do they gate UI? This matters for which views appear in a default/E2E configuration.

Return a detailed, factual report with EXACT strings (label text, aria-labels, role names, button names) that a Playwright test could use as locators. Quote the relevant JSX snippets. Do not speculate — only report what the code at origin/main actually says. If something does not exist (e.g. no Opportunity Landscape), say so explicitly.
I'll explore the repository systematically, starting with the branch structure and the key files.

# Running The Living Studio

**The Living Studio** is the conversational GUI for Outcome-Driven Innovation:
an interactive Opportunity Landscape, Universal Job Map, WYSIWYG Impact
Simulation, and Causal Lineage inspection, paired with an autonomous agent
connected to the MCP server.

The Studio runs three ways locally, plus a hosted deployment. All of them serve
the same SPA, which talks only to the sidecar on `http://127.0.0.1:8100` — the
SPA never contacts MCP or the LLM directly.

## Architecture

```text
┌────────────────────────────┐  /api (JSON)  ┌───────────────────────────────┐
│  Living Studio SPA         │ ────────────▶ │  apps/studio-api (sidecar)    │
│  React + TS + Vite         │  /api/chat    │  FastAPI on 127.0.0.1:8100    │
│  (browser or Tauri webview)│ ◀──────────── │  - config / health / canvas   │
└────────────────────────────┘  SSE stream   │  - steps / outcomes (via MCP) │
                                             │  - /api/chat (LLM tool-loop)  │
                                             └───────────────┬───────────────┘
                                                             │ MCP (HTTP)
                                                             ▼
                                             ┌───────────────────────────────┐
                                             │  apps/mcp-server :8000/mcp    │
                                             └───────────────────────────────┘
                                                             ▲
                                                             │ OpenAI-compatible
                                             ┌───────────────┴───────────────┐
                                             │  Your local LLM backend       │
                                             └───────────────────────────────┘
```

## Interface

The Studio opens as a conversation, not a dashboard.

| Surface | What it does |
|---|---|
| **First-run tour** | A four-step, skippable welcome on the very first visit: what the studio is, which of four starting points you want, the live state of your sidecar/MCP/model (with inline repair when the model is down), and the first move. Finishing opens the chosen surface; **Name the job** hands off to the context conversation. Replay it from **Settings → Replay the welcome tour**. |
| **First run** | A short conversation in the chat, not a form: what you are building, who feels the problem, the job they are trying to get done, then where it hurts. One question at a time, with a reflection before the next ask, quick replies, and **Explore on my own** always visible. Skipping is allowed; answers and progress are kept as a draft. Re-open it any time with `/start`, the home stage's context pill, or Settings. |
| **Hero** | One rotating headline above the composer: a greeting (time of day, plus your name if you set one in Settings), the product/job you set up, what is already on the canvas, or what the studio can do. It cycles every few seconds and stays still under `prefers-reduced-motion`. |
| **Suggestion pills** | Below the headline. Some start a conversation (define a job, simulate a bet, capture what a customer said), others open a lens (landscape, job map). They change as the canvas fills up. |
| **Composer** | Docked at the bottom of the transcript. `Enter` sends, `Shift`+`Enter` adds a line, `Cmd/Ctrl`+`K` focuses it, and `/` opens the command palette. The send button becomes a stop button while a reply streams. |
| **Bar** | The only persistent chrome: home, new conversation, catch-up, live model status, and settings. There is no navigation drawer to compete with the thread. |
| **Rail** | Above the conversation, and only once the thread has produced something: `Landscape · N`, `Job map · N`, `Evidence · N`. Every item is derived from the canvas, so the strip is a record of the work rather than a fixed menu. |
| **Lens** | A view docks to the right of the thread on wide screens and becomes a full-height sheet on narrow ones. # Running The Living Studio

**The Living Studio** is the conversational GUI for Outcome-Driven Innovation:
an interactive Opportunity Landscape, Universal Job Map, WYSIWYG Impact
Simulation, and Causal Lineage inspection, paired with an autonomous agent
connected to the MCP server.
